I have been working this land in Quzhou for 55 years. I know what grows and what doesn't. My wheat-maize rotation runs on 5 mu — same ground, two crops a year. The other 3 mu I keep in cotton for cash income. With just the two of us at home now, I do not overextend myself.

For the wheat, I plant in October when the soil cools. I use the improved variety I have been buying from the village supply cooperative for years — it is reliable and I trust it. I water four times: once before the ground freezes, again at jointing, then at heading, then when the grain is filling. I put down base fertilizer before planting and top-dress with urea at jointing. I spray herbicide early, then watch for rust and powdery mildew in spring — two or three spray rounds.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant maize on the same 5 mu without plowing — just go in with the planter. Hybrid seed gives better yield and I have used it for many years now. Maize does not need as much work. I fertilize twice, irrigate maybe three times if rain is short, and check for corn borer in late summer.

The cotton on my 3 mu is the most work — I have to top the plants, thin the seedlings, and spray for bollworm and aphids many times through summer. I plow that ground in spring before planting. I start harvesting in September and keep picking through October.
